I've been farming this same land since I was a young man helping my father. In Quzhou, everyone around here grows winter wheat and summer corn on rotation — it's what the land is suited for, it's what the market buys, and I know how to do it properly. I'm not going to experiment.

My land is about 8 mu. I plant wheat every October after the rains, harvest in June, then put in corn right after on the same fields. That's two crops a year from the same soil — you can't ask for more than that.

For wheat I use improved seed from the county seed station, not the old varieties. I learned that lesson — the certified seed gives better heads and resists lodging better when wind comes. I'll apply base fertilizer before planting, then come back in spring to top-dress with urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: before winter sets in, again at jointing, and once more at heading. Fewer irrigations would worry me — I've seen neighbors lose yield going dry at filling stage. I'll spray herbicide in autumn, then fungicide and aphicide in spring when rust and aphids show up.

For corn I use hybrid seed, same as always. I do rotary tillage right after wheat harvest because I need to get seed in the ground fast — the season is short. Corn needs less hand-holding than wheat so I irrigate twice and spray twice.

I expect roughly 450 jin per mu on wheat and 550 on corn. That's what a normal year gives me here.
